import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Inverse Galois problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem)
-/

namespace InverseGalois

structure GaloisRealization.{u, v} (K : Type u) (G : Type v) [Field K] [Group G] where
  -- Every Galois extension of `K : Type u` injects into `AlgebraicClosure K : Type u`.
  -- We therefore lose no generality assuming `L : Type u`.
  L : Type u
  to_field : Field L
  to_algebra : Algebra K L
  to_isGalois : IsGalois K L
  iso : G ≃* (L ≃ₐ[K] L)

/--
Say a group `G` is realizable over a field `K` if it
is isomorphic to the Galois group of a Galois extension
of `K`
-/
class IsRealizable (K G : Type*) [Field K] [Group G] where
  exists_realization : Nonempty (GaloisRealization K G)

/--
The **Inverse Galois Problem**: every finite group is
isomorphic to the Galois group of a Galois extension of the
rationals.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite cyclic group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.cyclic
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] [IsCyclic G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite abelian group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.abelian
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G] :
    IsRealizable ℚ G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite symmetric group is realizable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.symmetric_group
    {S : Type*} [Fintype S] :
    IsRealizable ℚ (S ≃ S) := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite group is realisable over the field of rational functions
with complex coefficients.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.complex_rational_functions
    {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable (RatFunc ℂ) G := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite group is realisable over the field of rational functions
with coefficients `K`, where `K` is any field of characteristic 0.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem inverse_galois_problem.variants.complex_function_field
    {G K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] [Fintype G] [Group G] :
    IsRealizable (RatFunc K) G := by
  sorry

end InverseGalois

findings.description: The coefficient field is missing the hypothesis `[IsAlgClosed K]`. Lines 97–98 quantify over every characteristic-zero field, whereas the cited result concerns algebraically closed coefficient fields. This is a substantive strengthening: specializing to `K = ℚ` asserts realizability of every finite group over ℚ(t), which would imply the open inverse Galois problem over ℚ by Hilbert irreducibility. A Lean experiment confirms this specialization is accepted and independently proves `¬ IsAlgClosed ℚ`. The docstring repeats the same overgeneralization.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, “Inverse Galois problem”, §Partial results (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem#Partial_results), states realizability “over function fields in one variable over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.” The same section describes specialization from ℚ(t) to ℚ using Hilbert’s irreducibility theorem, and the introduction records the general problem over ℚ as unsolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `[IsAlgClosed K]` to the hypotheses and require algebraic closedness in the docstring: `{G K : Type*} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [CharZero K] [Fintype G] [Group G] : IsRealizable (RatFunc K) G`. The `research solved` category is appropriate for this corrected statement.

reformulations.difference: Realizability uses a bundled extension whose underlying type lies in the base field’s universe, without explicitly requiring the extension to be finite-dimensional.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite G, the supplied group isomorphism makes the automorphism group finite, so IsGalois.finiteDimensional_of_finite gives a finite extension. Conversely, every Galois extension is algebraic and embeds into AlgebraicClosure K, which lies in K’s universe. Passing to the embedding’s range and conjugating automorphisms preserves the realization. In /workspace/review/equivalences.lean I proved IsRealizable K G equivalent to existence of a finite Galois intermediate field of AlgebraicClosure K with automorphism group isomorphic to G, and separately constructed a realization from an extension in an arbitrary universe.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses ℂ(t), while the source states realizability over every one-variable complex function field.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The universal assertion for all finite groups over ℂ(t) implies the source’s broader formulation. A one-variable function field F is finite over a rational subfield R ≅ ℂ(t). For a finite group G, choose m with 2^m > [F:R], and realize G^m by E/R. Then Gal(EF/F) identifies with a subgroup H of G^m of index at most [F:R]. If every coordinate projection of H had proper image, its index would be at least 2^m. Thus some projection H → G is surjective, and its kernel’s fixed field realizes G over F. The reverse implication follows by taking F = ℂ(t).

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_Galois_problem (revision 1372008347; full article, including variants, status, and references)
Local Mathlib: Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean, especially IsGalois and IsGalois.finiteDimensional_of_finite.
review.notes: Checked both definitions and all six theorem statements. No independent stale-status issue was found: the last theorem needs its source hypothesis restored, rather than merely a category change. The other five theorem statements and their status tags agree with the source. Independent Lean checks in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean and /workspace/review/domain_check.lean compile without errors or sorry dependencies. They cover universe restriction, finiteness of realizations, trivial groups, and symmetric groups on empty and singleton types; computed permutation-group orders for sizes 0–4 were 1, 1, 2, 6, 24. The reviewed file’s hash matches the specified commit; all experiments were kept outside the repository.

submission.summary: Added `[IsAlgClosed K]` and updated the docstring to require an algebraically closed coefficient field of characteristic zero. Preserved the existing category and AMS attributes and left all other declarations unchanged. The required Lean compilation succeeds with only the permitted `sorry` warnings.
